evidence: RUNTIME HALF (passes). I checked each fact on the quality-checks.md #4 list against the brief/notes and against tests/test.sh, which is byte-identical to the template. Path: instruction.md:15 'Put the application in /app'. Start command: instruction.md:15 'It must start with node /app/server.js' and integration.md:5, matching test.sh APP_ENTRY=/app/server.js. Port: instruction.md:15 'listen on port 3000 (honour PORT if it's set)' and integration.md:5 '0.0.0.0'. These match test.sh PORT="3000", its 127.0.0.1:3000 probes and the http://localhost:3000 URL in every prompt. Storage: instruction.md:15 'keep its durable data in /app/app.db, honouring DB_PATH when that is set' and integration.md:7-8, matching test.sh DB_PATH=$APP_DB (/app/app.db or the writable-copy fallback). Health: instruction.md:15 'expose GET /api/health as a check that never touches the database' and integration.md:9-10, matching the test.sh /api/health probe. Seed: instruction.md:15 '/assets/seed_data.json'; instruction.md:17 'Load ... once, start with no shipped database, and keep new work across restarts'; hireops_rules.md section 9 gives read-marker semantics and says the candidate wording and page size are in the seed file. Accounts: instruction.md:19 gives the shared password Hireops!2026 and all ten emails with roles, matching app_context.md Accounts and the seed users. The seed users also carry the display names the criteria use. Launch conditions: integration.md:16-23 and hireops_rules.md section 8 state the different working directory, the locked-down user, the writable copy, the symlink limits and the only env vars (PATH, HOME, NODE_PATH, PORT, DB_PATH). These match test.sh env -i, setpriv uid 65534, the APP_COPY fallback and its symlink refusal. Dependencies: instruction.md:15 and integration.md:3-4 say Express and better-sqlite3 come through NODE_PATH and nothing should be installed. Fixed clock: N-A. No criterion grades an absolute date or time. Seed timestamps (2026-07) only order seeded history, and newest-first Activity and message order need only a monotonic real clock. Network: public. instruction.md:15 allows CDN fonts and scripts and forbids only an outside data service. Prompts use localhost only, so lesson 13 is satisfied. Minor note: instruction.md:17 says /assets is unavailable at runtime, but test.sh chmods /assets and task.toml artifacts include it. The brief is stricter than the runtime, so this cannot mis-grade a conforming app. DELIVERABLE HALF (one gap). Applying lesson 1, I walked every criterion in the 2 gates, 12 functional, 5 polish and 5 visual rows against the brief and notes. Almost every graded leg has a public sentence. Examples: 409 plus who made the change (rules section 3 'Two people at once'); bottom-of-stage placement and board-order bulk landing (section 3); Interview capacity including undo overfill (section 3 'Undo'); focus kept on the refused card (section 3 'Shown at once'); statuses 401/403/404 (section 1); the six candidate wordings plus team and title (section 7); 30-message pages and anchor preservation (section 6); unread and seen definitions, including that an observer never counts (section 6); reply drafts isolated per person and per conversation (instruction.md:7 and rules section 6 Drafts); the sign-in prompt when a session ends (section 6 Drafts); a failed send kept and explained (section 6 Messages); live updates within 15 s without disturbing typing, focus, the open card or scroll (instruction.md:5, rules section 5); plain-text messages (section 6); email-field refusal keeping typed values, and case-insensitive duplicates (section 2); places a whole number from 1 to 50 and the manager drawn from hiring-manager accounts (section 2); desktop-only craft (instruction.md:11). GAP: tests/scored/polish/judge.toml hro_pol_session_resume (weight 2) has Rafael type 'an unsaved note on one of your cards, sign out, sign in as Mei Lin on this browser and open ... that card: both boxes are empty', and the row 'Fails if ... Mei sees either of Rafael's drafts'. The only public sentence on note drafts is hireops_rules.md section 3 'Internal notes': 'If I'm halfway through typing a note and haven't saved it, keep it for me on that browser until I do.' The brief states per-person draft privacy only for replies: instruction.md:7 'A reply I have not sent ... nobody else who signs in on that browser sees it' and hireops_rules.md section 6 Drafts 'Nobody else who signs in on that browser sees any of mine.' Since isolation is spelled out for replies and left out for notes, a reasonable builder can treat note drafts as per-card browser drafts. The criterion then grades an unstated requirement. Two weaker observations are not counted as defects. hro_intake_restart refuses a blank job title on the basis of 'A job has a title' (rules section 2), a reasonable implied requirement. The gates' 'reload, still signed in' check rests on the session wording in rules sections 1 and 6 and on the house sign-in convention (a SKILL known false positive). The raw evidence index hashes verify. That index holds only scripted golden observations and does not bear on this source-level row. No configured judge run, Oracle score or model score exists, and none is claimed.
counterexample: Take a conforming app that stores an unsaved internal-note draft in localStorage keyed only by application id. It satisfies 'keep it for me on that browser until I do' and survives Rafael's sign-out and sign-in. Reply drafts are scoped per user, as the brief explicitly requires. In hro_pol_session_resume, Rafael signs out and Mei signs in on the same browser and opens that card. Her note box shows Rafael's unsaved note, so the row fails ('Mei sees either of Rafael's drafts'). The app loses 2 of 9.5 polish weight (about 0.042 reward) for a requirement the brief never states for notes. This is an under-specification fairness defect, not a false-pass risk: it does not help a broken app pass.
suggested_fix: In hireops_rules.md section 3 'Internal notes', extend the sentence in the requester's voice. Example: 'If I'm halfway through typing a note and haven't saved it, keep it for me on that browser until I do, even if I get signed out; like my replies, it's mine, so nobody else who signs in there sees it.' Alternatively, drop the note half of the Mei-privacy leg from hro_pol_session_resume. After the edit, re-review the rows it touches (1, 2, 5, 6, 27, 31).
